title: Choose Clarifi's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Payslip Arithmetic direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Payslip Arithmetic
options.lineage: NZ payslips and IRD form arithmetic on carbonless triplicate paper
options.thesis: Your budget is a payslip: every line shows the sum that produced it, so nothing on the page is a number you have to trust.
materials: carbonless triplicate paper (white, canary, pink copies)
options.viewport: One white sheet, full width. Top band: statement period and a three-copy tab (Card · Mine · Partner) like the white/canary/pink sheets of a triplicate set. Below, the six buckets as payslip lines: description, rule code, card amount × share = mine, each sum written out. Right margin: the rules that fired, as numbered box codes. Primary action, 'Import statement', is a filled carbon-blue box at the sheet's top right.
options.risk: Can read as bureaucratic if the ruling is heavy or the type timid; the arithmetic must feel like reassurance, not a tax form.

raised.raise: A row changed by a new rule moves to its new bucket in place and holds a canary highlight until you scroll past it.
Two rules matching one row cross-hatch that row instead of silently taking the first match; the conflict is visible and resolvable inline.
Every rule, box and divider is a true 1px hairline on an 8px grid; no shadows, no radius, no fills except the three copy tints.
States are printed marks: a share box is hollow at 0%, half-filled at 50%, filled at 100%, struck through when a row is excluded.
Two type sizes only across all tables; rank is carried by weight, case and the tint of the copy sheet.

regions.label: six bucket lines, each with its arithmetic

options.label: Flat Whiteboard Tally
options.lineage: the shared-flat kitchen whiteboard: columns per person, bills tallied, items struck when settled
options.thesis: The shared card as the flat's whiteboard: one column per person, each line written to whoever owes it.
options.viewport: Three marker columns (Card, Mine, Partner) across the whole width; each transaction is a line written into a column, bills split across two. Rules are magnets pinned at the top of each column.
options.risk: Familiar: close to Splitwise and bill-split apps, so it reads as a known category rather than Clarifi's own.

options.label: Boarding Pass and Gate Board
options.thesis: Transactions as a departure board: rows rerank by bucket and a changed row stays lit until noticed.
options.viewport: A ranked board of transactions in fixed columns; the statement itself as a segmented boarding pass above.
options.case: Fuses well on clarity: live rerank with persistent change state is exactly what a new rule does to rows. Loses on audience: a household budget is not an airport.
options.risk: Reads as novelty when the board grammar is loosened.

options.label: Exposure Record Zone Sheets
options.lineage: darkroom printers' exposure records on tracing-paper overlays
options.thesis: Rules as translucent overlays on the statement; overlapping rules cross-hatch to show conflict.
options.viewport: The statement as a backlit field; each rule a sheet laid over it, hatched regions showing which rows it claims.
options.case: Wins on one axis: conflict rendered as cross-hatching is the clearest treatment of overlapping rules on the table. Loses on audience: a darkroom means nothing to a household budgeter.
options.risk: Grey-ramp world reads cold for money.

options.label: Design Annual Plate Section
options.lineage: design annual plate pages with registration marks
options.thesis: The budget as a plate section with registration furniture.
options.viewport: Buckets as plates in a 12-column grid with crosshair corners.
options.case: Loses both: designers' annuals are not the audience's world and registration marks say nothing about money.
options.kept: Hairline ruling discipline: every rule 1px on an 8px grid.

options.label: Centre Rail Reference Setting
options.lineage: scholarly reference editions with a central key rail
options.thesis: The budget as a reference edition with a vermilion rail of keys.
options.viewport: Two text columns around a rail of rule keys.
options.case: Loses both: a scholarly edition is foreign to the audience and two-column prose fights tabular money.
options.kept: States as printed marks: hollow, half, filled, struck.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: Buckets as raked glass slides on a goldenrod bed.
options.viewport: A lateral rack of raked slides, one per bucket.
options.case: Loses both: 11-degree rake fights tabular figures and the airline world is not the household's.
options.kept: Two type sizes only; rank by weight and case.
options.risk: Rake makes numbers hard to read.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Buckets as ranked mascots with name plates.
options.viewport: A pastel grid of bucket mascots.
options.case: Loses both: mascots undercut trust in money figures and the audience is not collecting characters.
options.kept: One flat colour per bucket, used only as a ribbon, never as fill.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The fintech dashboard everyone ships: sidebar, KPI cards, donut by category, transactions table.
canonCard.viewport: Four KPI cards, a donut, a bar chart, a paginated table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every budgeting app by design.
